messages.body_plain:
You may like to try Version 2.6.27 r99:

> install.packages("rattle", repos="http://rattle.togaware.com", type="source")

I've reinstated rattle_macosx.ui for Mac OS/X.

Regards,
Graham

On Wednesday, April 3, 2013 6:07:33 AM UTC+11, timeitself wrote:
> I have the same problem and the dokondr's receipt it's working fine for me. It is actually the only way I have right now to run Rattle on my Mac.
> This issue started today, after I updated Rattle (now 2.6.26 r77).
>
> Carlo

>
> On Friday, February 1, 2013 5:00:14 PM UTC-5, Graham Williams wrote:
> > The "rm(list=ls())" is needed because you would have saved the R workspace on exiting R - and that workspace is automatically reloaded when you start R next time. Unfortunately, some saved objects interfered with Rattle causing the issues you saw I think (though later versions of Rattle have attempted to rectify that and no longer saves ponjects in the user workspace). Never saving the default workspace avoids the problem (as does removing the workspace when you start up R as in your rm() command).
> >
> > The use of rattle_macosx.ui is a mystery. That was an old GUI to get around some Mac OS/X bugs that I believe have now been fixed. I'm not sure what the problem could be - do you still need that after cleaning out your workspace? What happens if you don't do that step?
> >
> > Graham Williams
> > http://togaware.com
> >
> >
> > On 1 February 2013 23:11, dokondr <dok...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > Finally after endless attempts I have found solution to this problem !!!
> > > You need to do the following steps in this *exact order* and *every time* you start R:
> > >
> > > > rm(list=ls())
> > > > library(rattle)
> > > Rattle: A free graphical interface for data mining with R.
> > > Version 2.6.26 r55 Copyright (c) 2006-2013 Togaware Pty Ltd.
> > > Type 'rattle()' to shake, rattle, and roll your data.
> > > > crv$rattleUI <- "rattle_macosx.ui"
> > > > rattle()
> > >
> > > The good news is that once you are in running  R environment, you can exit and start rattle() many times, to your hart content, without resetting ui variable.
> > > But once you exit R, you need to repeat the above steps within new R session.
> > >
> > > Uff.......

messages.body_plain:
Thanks for the posts re Rattle and RGtk2 on Mac OS/X. Please report the R and Rattle version (output of rattleInfo()). The latest release is Version 2.6.27 r100:

> install.packages("rattle", repos="http://rattle.togaware.com", type="source")

Also something to try:

> library(rattle)
> crv$rattleUI <- "rattle_macosx.ui"
> rattle()

or

> library(rattle)
> crv$rattleUI <- "rattle.ui"
> rattle()

It is not yet clear where the problem is (not having access to Mac OS/X does not help the debugging...)

Rattle itself does not install GTK+ but relies on RGtk2 for that - Rattle calls on RGtk2 to be installed which in turn installs GTK+.

Could the problem be that there are multiple versions of GTK installed? Perhaps try removing all GTK installations and then reinstall the latest.

Also, I would be keen to know if the following works:

Graham Williams
http://togaware.com

> On Mac-OS there seems to be a mismatch between the version of GTK+ (namely 2.18.5) that is installed by Rattle versus the version that RGtk2 is actually looking for. Look at this diagnostic:
